integrationPoints.responsibility: The OMP adapter owns its paired askDialog field convention and validates answers before completing the session-owned request. The provider-neutral question contract exposes an optional combined multi-select/custom capability; activity normalization, saved drafts and the existing composer preserve it. Ordinary ACP and Droid conventions retain their existing mapping. Gateway send failures preserve the requested target and structured non-dispatch reasons without relaxing cross-thread authority.

Static registry owns Expert/MCP navigation and search metadata. settingsPages lazily assembles existing panels with route context from workbench/host/settings. The native route retains its shell, canonical URL behavior and browser history; feature panels retain their existing dirty draft guard and cache. Global MCP operations pin their target/revisions and own a view generation so late results cannot mutate a different editor or confirmation.

wsRpc owns authenticated connection context, admission, requireOwner and the distinct rpcEffect/expertRpcEffect error mappings. A static host assembly supplies Expert/MCP handlers using the existing Workbench runtime and projection read capability. Web feature consumers use the existing NativeApi server ExpertClient type subset without a second transport/cache. Wire method names, schemas and durable ownership remain unchanged. Instance-scoped preview delegates a narrow read-only compatibility request to ProviderService; owner authorization precedes native configuration inspection.

The existing orchestration command path validates the selected Expert and prepares an immutable snapshot before committing thread creation. Provider startup reads the thread binding and enforces required connection preflight; failures continue to block startup with the existing command errors.

Resume reuses the persisted provider runtime payload and the thread's pinned Expert snapshot. It does not resolve the current Expert definition when restoring an existing session; provider-specific application remains owned by each adapter. Claude and OMP verify immutable native projections and return application receipts. Cursor-only native forks remain stopped with the inherited snapshots until their first start; only a verified running generation may persist applied records.

The existing Gateway resolves only tools listed in the immutable Expert snapshot, scopes connected clients to the Gateway session, and closes them when the session is revoked or released. Capability and RPC registration stay in their existing owners.

The thread-created event carries the Expert binding through the native projector, projection query and web store. Authoritative null bindings continue to clear the client projection after replay or hydration.

Expert-owned immutable packages and source pointers are accessed through owner RPC and the narrow ExpertClient. A shared in-process stateDir writer queue serializes package publication/removal with Expert revisions and task snapshot publication. Deletion scans all definitions, retained revisions and snapshots (including accepted Hub bindings), failing closed on unknown ownership. V2 snapshots pin selected entries without copying skills; references retain their original owner. Host provider lifecycle composes and verifies catalog instructions and persists submission receipts through expert ledger migration 6. The existing Settings parent and composer own navigation, subscriptions, draft promotion and permissions; draft skill identities are bound to the accepted snapshot before dispatch. BMad presets and workspace inspection stay outside generic storage. The existing Expert editor owns the unified skill picker draft; discovery and path preview use existing host capabilities. Apply validates and imports immutable packages before updating only the draft, while explicit Save retains Expert revision conflict checks. Reuse copies saved skill selections without mutating the source Expert; async completions are scoped to the active connection and dialog. The boundary check covers declared direct imports, not runtime permissions or transitive isolation. The one-time switch runs through authenticated owner RPC with a reviewed digest and durable backup/progress; native stop, cancel and delete own task history and eventual purge; the switch conservatively retains snapshots named in its reviewed plan and reports retained artifacts. Cleanup rechecks references under the lifecycle lock; Claude projections are scoped to managed metadata, while OMP temporary files remain adapter-owned. Expert task admission preflights the effective worktree or project workspace before binding a snapshot.

Expert definitions, connection configuration and immutable snapshots use private files below the selected state directory. Thread bindings remain in the native projection schema and applied runtime records remain in the existing SQLite repository. WB-02 owns its migration ledger and read-only upgrade plan; integrated SqlitePersistence startup uses the existing connection/lifecycle lock and passes that plan through native pre-migration backup, resume and explicit restore. This native integration is required because the extension changes projection/table schema and must share the host's single SQLite ownership and recovery point. On tested source SHA 858, three synthetic file-backed SQLite rehearsal scenarios passed: successful startup and failure/retry using the same backup ran through the pinned Bun harness; the restore CLI ran with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 in the actual packaged Workbench Electron 43.4.1 executable and exited 0. The raw rehearsal report SHA-256 is e44bf0a069bc01f4a270e3a758a78835f6dcdfaec2a127c15787cc81fa13d5ef and its audit SHA-256 is bdd5506cea0f46b9e772428b60f45e71ffbe6453335137869d475938cf08eebc. These source-858 scenarios used synthetic data only, did not access a user database, and do not prove ordinary Electron startup/upgrade. A later independent rehearsal on source SHA f2483e077a100f8a7e775a65d7b20d59858bf8cc also passed three synthetic scenarios: the first two used the pinned Bun harness and the third ran the packaged Workbench Electron 43.4.1 restore CLI in ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 mode (raw report SHA-256 8a31b94b8edf521a9592f452c3950598a700d90554ef7a48467c7a0be0913cf7). That result is source-bound and likewise does not prove ordinary Electron startup/upgrade or user-database migration. The official v0.9.2 migration history ends at 108; old fork rows 109/110 are recognized only by exact legacy identity and resulting schema, then adopted into local expert migration IDs, never treated as official published migrations. The v1.0.5 candidate uses the exact official native catalog through 135. Legacy Expert 109/110 and Context 111 are recognized by frozen identity and schema, audited in workbench_legacy_migration_adoptions and transferred atomically after the unified backup. Context uses context1 by importing the frozen Effect script; Expert IDs/checksums are unchanged. Recovery v3 binds each module progress and original identities to the existing snapshot; unexplainable old markers are preserved and rejected. Frozen Context recognition compares table DDL and the four delivery column definitions, including CHECK constraints, and rejects unknown objects attached to protected tables. The same read-only metadata query and pure validator are used by live startup and backup inspection; no trial writes validate a user database.

Static direct import check covers server/web workbench/features, existing server experts and named Expert/MCP, Space and Context Web surfaces, plus the exact migrated Space and project-context feature files below. New full native client, task store/router, database, Provider, orchestration, Gateway, auth, legacy project-context cache and Context persistence imports are refused. Host files assemble native capabilities. Exact retained imports below preserve established lifecycle and credential ownership. This guard is not runtime isolation or a transitive security check; registry/runtime/host assembly remain outside the feature scan.

Existing typed tool resolution and session ownership; no lifecycle relocation.

Native navigation blocking, save/discard/cancel and beforeunload remain one implementation.

Acceptance preflight receives the existing read-only Provider discovery capability and reuses native target validation; it does not start or switch runtimes. Native Gateway input errors preserve the existing typed failure surface.
The service owns only its independent-ledger collection and request tables on the host connection. Publication pointers and maintenance intents require the existing SQL transaction capability.
Receives the existing SqlClient; native config and roster writes participate in the same ambient transaction. No independent connection or executor.
Shared SqlClient only, for atomic plan, native task, receipt and outbox operations. No independent database or task scheduler.

integrationPoints.responsibility: The sidebar owns Space controller and route synchronization because those modules use native navigation, the task store and the established Space mutation capability. The Context host client exposes read-only legacy project-instructions cache access to Context feature consumers with shared contracts; ChatView and chat execution/automation modules remain host integrations for their existing context injection and prompt flows. Server wsRpc/runtime assembly owns authenticated Context RPC admission and error mapping, contextThreadDetails combines the repository with live execution evidence, OrchestrationEngine and ProjectionPipeline own replayable Context lifecycle, ProviderCommandReactor loads thread bindings and context sessions for execution, ProviderService applies runtime Context and records execution state, and ContextRepository owns Context SQL persistence. The existing projection service owns Space projection; the original 111_ContextV1 script remains frozen and is reused by the context1 ledger Effect; exact legacy tracker adoption shares the host connection, transaction, backup and recovery ownership, while active native 111 belongs to official GroupLibraryHosting. Contracts keep the shared Context wire schema. This records ownership only; wire behavior, lifecycle and persistence semantics remain in their existing implementations. Context capability negotiation distinguishes unknown, unsupported and supported. The existing WsTransport owns connection state and sessionVersion; its read-only host metadata fences shared query results and late asynchronous returns. Reconnect pauses Context writes immediately and resumes only after a real read in the current shared generation. Project autosave keeps the original API/data instance/project queue identity. Project and Space editors preserve dirty, pending and uncertain drafts across owner changes until explicit discard; Space reuses the existing draft guard and fields editor, including real close/navigation protection. A new owner cannot reuse a previous owner's draft or command attempt. Every actual Expert session start or native fork preflights required MCP before ProviderService admission; ordinary reuse keeps the existing lifecycle.

The migration guard verifies every active native script against the fixed official catalog, preserves the exact historical Context 111 path/identity/digest, and statically proves that context1 imports the frozen Effect in the active module catalog. The build source parser records separate Expert/Context high-water marks and rejects unknown or omitted effect sources. Historical 109/110/111 tracker identities are compatibility inputs to the exact audited adoption path, never additional native catalog entries. Missing upstream evidence blocks the check; no directory-wide exemptions apply.

Reuse existing typed props for picker and task controls. ChatView owns draft/thread identity, disabled state and handoff command; feature UI reads only ExpertClient capabilities. No empty wrapper, store duplication or transcript dispatch was introduced. Deep task binding remains in native orchestration. Composer Skill discovery reads the accepted Expert snapshot through ExpertClient for bound threads and reuses the existing Expert preview for unsent drafts. Accepted bindings take precedence; neither path falls back to the Harness catalog on empty, pending, or failed reads. Ordinary threads and native slash commands retain their existing discovery.

Hub coordinator creation resolves the target and immutable Expert binding before durable queue acceptance. The server-only orchestration dispatch context carries that binding; public tool/RPC payloads never authorize a binding. ProjectAgent resolves explicit Project Context sources and authenticated Hub identities. Key collections use bounded raw Git blob IO and a private index with commit-tree/CAS update-ref, bypassing content filters and commit hooks to preserve exact bytes; the extension-ledger SQL pointer/journal retains recovery ownership; workers publish/withdraw only their own collection and read authorized same-Hub publications. Existing RPC, Context, Library and Provider lifecycles remain the host seams. The boundary scan is static and does not prove runtime isolation.

The approved UI extends the native Project menu, Hub cards/rows and Library only. Sidebar and onboarding own native create/link/configure/navigation capabilities; the existing Hub overview supplies accepted Expert names. Library consumes typed publication metadata and pinned reads through the existing authenticated NativeApi subset. WorkspaceFilePreview accepts read-only pinned content without live-path fallback. Native chat layout, subscriptions, split picker, permissions, file preview/history and lifecycle remain host-owned. Static boundary checks cover the declared pure derivations and backend services, not runtime isolation.

The native Sidebar, ChatView, Space route helpers and Context dialog remain host integrations. Hub worker ownership is resolved from server-confirmed membership and Hub Space assignment so the same thread lands in a consistent Hub/Space surface; the pure navigation derivations remain static-scanned. The read-only hubReferenceClient exposes authenticated NativeApi discovery with connection generation, and useHubComposerReferences fences query results to that generation. Shared hubReferences owns the canonical versioned mention URI parser/builder used by composition, persistence, display and server projection. The pure deliverable presentation helper groups active publications by accepted Expert identity and source work for both Library and the composer chooser; files retain pinned-version selection metadata, while missing entries remain visible/disabled and withdrawn collections are excluded. Context details render v2 Space-only and Hub-background snapshots while retaining v1 Space-to-Project snapshots. Native chat state, routing, persistence and runtime authorization remain host-owned. Static coverage is a direct-import check of declared feature sources, not transitive or runtime isolation.

Native project metadata and event replay own Hub Space membership; ContextRepository resolves explicit source Project or standalone Hub Space and freezes versioned snapshots without rewriting v1 history. The authenticated user RPC and coordinator catalogue resolve the explicit target, source project, or Hub in the same order as dispatch, check the creation allowlist, and return the effective target per Expert. Runtime terminal activities settle managed work independently of Git checkpoints; current durable work/result/inbox facts drive digest state, with typed source navigation. Committed publication/withdrawal/path maintenance emits deliverables-changed on the native Hub stream; Library and composer own reference-counted subscriptions and re-fetch on reconnect. ProviderCommandReactor supplies the authenticated current-thread capability to the Hub reference projector before Provider startup. The projector consumes reserved app references, validates same-Hub publication metadata and emits bounded read instructions without file bodies; ordinary provider mentions continue through native projection. HubWork source extraction copies references only from durable human messages. The existing work repository and immutable Expert store supply publication identity and work titles through a narrow resolver injected by ProjectAgentService. Static boundary coverage adds the pure URI parser and capability-driven projector; host lifecycle, SQL, native projection, and runtime authorization remain owned by their existing modules and require behavioral tests. Participant discovery reads only ProjectAgentConfig.expertIds; settings use the existing authenticated ExpertClient catalogue. Workbench migration expert/5 owns roster rows; ProjectAgentRepository replaces them transactionally with config revision. New Hub work acceptance rechecks revision and membership after replay lookup; accepted work keeps its frozen binding. The host-only resolveParticipatingExpert validates current Coordinator mentions and supplies trusted names. These seams grant no Agent roster-write capability. Worker context assembly uses an internal typed section envelope; the provider reactor owns generation-scoped delivery receipts and retires them on compaction, reset or failure. Fixed direct plan inputs are captured in HubWork creationSpec by the existing plan host. No context receipt authorizes tools or changes pinned Context/Expert bindings.

Owner-authorized configuration and plan RPCs persist immutable presets, configuration snapshots, candidates, reviews, decisions, directed input requests and execution intents. Host adapters bind plans to native Goal/Task/HubWork records and gate queue admission, worker startup and provider session restore. Directed answers resume only their original attempt through the existing outbox and native follow-up admission; they do not approve scope or bypass sandbox policy. Web features project read-only progress and business actions into the native transcript; the native composer draft store retains isolated reply drafts through a narrow host adapter. T3 revision impact analysis is preparatory and grants no execution or carry-forward authority. Static boundary coverage does not prove real provider execution or process recovery.
